subject: english
question: Find the part with an error: She asked (A) / me whether did I (B) / know the answer. (C)
explanation: Reported question needs normal order: 'whether I knew'.

subject: english
question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: To cut corners.
options: To do something cheaply by skipping proper procedure
explanation: It implies neglecting thoroughness to save time or money.

subject: english
question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 8)
options: Reason for him to resign was due because ill health.
The reason why he resigned is because of ill health.
He resigned because he was ill.
The reason he resigned is due because ill health.
explanation: Only option B avoids redundancy and faulty constructions.

subject: english
question: Improve the part in capitals: The report, together with the supporting documents, ARE on your desk.
explanation: The subject is 'report'; 'together with' does not make it plural.

subject: english
question: Improve the part in capitals: The CEO, WHO'S decisions were widely criticised, finally resigned.
explanation: Possessive 'whose' is needed, not 'who is'.

subject: english
question: The speaker's _____ delivery failed to _____ the restless audience.
explanation: A monotonous delivery cannot captivate an audience.

subject: english
question: Find the part with an error: Not only the (A) / officers but also the (B) / clerk were present at the meeting. (C)
explanation: The verb agrees with the nearer subject 'clerk', so 'was'.

subject: english
question: Find the part with an error: It is high time (A) / the management took (B) / strict action against defaulters. (C)
explanation: 'It is high time' correctly takes the simple past.

subject: english
question: The villagers, _____ by repeated broken promises, were in no mood to _____ the official's assurances.
explanation: Broken promises disillusion people, so they will not trust.

subject: english
question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: He was an OBSTINATE negotiator who rarely yielded.
explanation: Obstinate means stubborn; pliable means yielding.

subject: english
question: Choose the correct meaning of the phrasal verb: Their plan to expand abroad FELL THROUGH.
explanation: Fall through means come to nothing.

subject: english
question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. Remarkably, he finished the paper and secured a place on the merit list.
Q. Doctors advised complete rest, but he insisted on attending.
R. On the morning of the test, however, he fell seriously ill.
S. Rohit had prepared for the examination for nearly two years.
explanation: Preparation, illness, insistence, outcome.

subject: english
question: Improve the part in capitals: Each of the players HAVE scored a goal.
explanation: 'Each' takes a singular verb: 'has'.

subject: english
question: Improve the part in capitals: If I WOULD HAVE KNOWN the truth, I would have acted differently.
explanation: Third conditional if-clause takes past perfect.

subject: english
question: Choose the word closest in meaning to the word in capitals: The auditor's findings CORROBORATED the whistle-blower's claims.
explanation: Corroborate means to support with evidence.

subject: english
question: The treaty was signed _____ opposition from hardliners, _____ the moderates hailed it as historic.
explanation: 'Despite' plus 'while' gives the right contrast.

subject: english
question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. Over the long term, it also raises the risk of heart disease.
Q. Sleep deprivation affects far more than one's mood.
R. Studies link it to weaker memory and slower reaction times.
S. Adults are therefore advised to sleep seven to nine hours each night.
explanation: Statement, short-term effects, long-term effect, advice.

subject: english
question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: To be at loggerheads.
explanation: It means quarrelling or disagreeing sharply.

subject: english
question: Find the part with an error: One should (A) / always keep their (B) / promises. (C)
explanation: The pronoun must agree with 'one': 'one's promises'.

subject: english
question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 11)
options: She is fond of to sing.
explanation: 'Fond of' takes a gerund.

subject: english
question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: To pass the buck.
options: To shift responsibility to someone else
explanation: It means avoiding blame by handing responsibility on.

subject: english
question: Choose the word closest in meaning to the word in capitals: The regulator's silence was a TACIT admission of the lapse.
explanation: Tacit means understood without being stated.

subject: english
question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: To throw in the towel.
options: To admit defeat and give up
explanation: It comes from boxing and means surrender.

subject: english
question: Improve the part in capitals: The teacher, along with her students, HAS GONE on an excursion.
explanation: The sentence is correct as it stands.

subject: english
question: The bank has decided to _____ the interest rates, _____ the burden on borrowers.
explanation: Cutting rates eases the burden.

subject: english
question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 1)
options: Each of the clerks has submitted his own form.
He is more taller than any other boy in his class.
Neither of the two proposals were accepted.
The scenery of the hills are breathtaking.
explanation: 'Each' takes a singular verb and pronoun.

subject: english
question: Improve the part in capitals: The director along with his friends WERE invited to the function.
explanation: The subject is the singular 'director'.

subject: english
question: Find the part with an error: Despite he was ill, (A) / he attended the (B) / meeting to present the report. (C)
explanation: 'Despite' cannot introduce a clause; use 'Although he was ill' or 'Despite his illness'.

subject: english
question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. Within a week, tankers began arriving twice a day.
Q. The village council had long ignored the problem of drinking water.
R. Yet this relief was only temporary, and the council still has no permanent plan.
S. When the wells ran dry in April, the residents finally marched to the block office.
explanation: Background, protest, response, then the 'yet' caveat.

subject: english
question: Choose the word closest in meaning to the word in capitals: The mediator tried to PLACATE the angry customers.
explanation: Placate means to calm.
